title: Rethinking Colorectal Histopathology Classification: Style-Aware and Density-Guided Open-Set Domain Adaptation
content: In computational pathology, deployed histopathology models frequently encounter variations in staining protocols and scanning devices, as well as tissue categories that are absent from the training distribution. In this study, we address these challenges under the Open-Set Domain Adaptation (OSDA) setting, where a labeled source domain is adapted to an unlabeled target domain containing both known categories shared with the source domain and unknown tissue categories. We propose SADG, a Style-Aware and Density-Guided framework that jointly addresses covariate and semantic shifts. For semantic shift, unlike existing OSDA methods that collapse all unknown samples into a single category and overlook the intrinsic density structure of the target domain, a GMM-based ClusterNet models the density structure of target features and constructs class-conditional prototypes characterizing the distribution of shared known classes. Based on these cluster-guided statistics, a Gaussian Mixturebased Energy Measurement (GEM) score is derived to quantify sample openness and is further calibrated via Extreme Value Theory (EVT) to estimate unknown-class probabilities without fixed thresholds. To mitigate covariate shift, a Style Rectification Module (SRM) is incorporated into the backbone to suppress appearance-induced domain discrepancies while preserving diagnostically relevant style information. Furthermore, reliable homogeneous target clusters guide the classifier toward learning shared known classes, while pseudo-unknown samples prevent unknown instances from collapsing into known-class regions. Experiments on the Kather-16 and Kather-19 colorectal histopathology datasets under three open-set configurations demonstrate that SADG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both known-class classification and unknown-class detection. Code is available at https://github.com/ReyhaneGhaffari/SADGOSDA.git.
